in_sanskrit.name: Saravana
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Saravana is derived from the Sanskrit word 'sarva', meaning 'all', 'whole', 'entire'. The suffix 'ana' means 'flowing', 'abundant', 'available'. Thus, Saravana means 'flowing with all', 'abundant with all', or 'available to all'. This name is often used in religious contexts and is associated with the god Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, learning, and wisdom.

data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Saravana highlights the concept of attaining divine blessings and spiritual victory in one's life. It symbolizes the triumph of the soul over material desires and worldly challenges. The assumption of the name Saravana is an affirmation of one's unwavering faith in the Divine and a determination to overcome any obstacles that may hinder spiritual growth. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal of human existence, which is to realize the True Self, beyond the transient illusions of the physical world.

historical_references.reference: Saravana is believed to be an avatar of the Hindu god Murugan, also known as Subramania or Kartikeya. He is often depicted with six heads and twelve hands.
historical_references.context: Saravana is a significant deity in the Tamil region of South India, particularly among the Saiva and Vaishnava sects. His worship is rooted in ancient Hindu mythology, which describes him as the god of war, love, and fertility.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Saravana can be found in the ancient Tamil text 'Agastya Samhita', where he is mentioned as the presiding deity of the month of Adi (July-August) in the Tamil calendar.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient Tamil civilization (circa 3rd Century BCE to 3rd Century CE)
historical_references.context: The Agastya Samhita is an important agricultural and astronomical text that provides guidance on various aspects of Tamil life, including farming and calendar calculations. The mention of Saravana as the presiding deity of a month underscores his role as a protector of agriculture and fertility.
